title: Did the brains get better? Round 3's eras against each other
withdrawn: Withdrawn unplayed on 12 November 2026, with the author's agreement, after an independent review (11 November): health, which chose its 21 worlds, runs against heredity, generations and fertility in round 3, and the family trees behind that choice counted births only, though conquests copy brains more often. Experiment 45 plays the same tournament with three coins on each era's world, on the worlds the evolution rank puts first and on the healthiest and least healthy.

thesis.claim: Round 3's shortlisted worlds got better early and had stopped getting better by the middle of their runs. In most of the 21 worlds the brains of every later era beat the brains of iteration 250 beyond a contest's own noise; against the brains of iteration 1,500, the eras after it do no better than that noise.
thesis.why: Round 3's worlds evolve fast and narrowly: hundreds of generations in 3,000 iterations, an effective population of about 14, and a line of descent that keeps moving a little beyond the noise (Candidates for open-ended evolution). The notebook's two longest worlds, of B2 with brains mixed at birth, climbed for 20,000 to 25,000 iterations and then only wandered (Every era against three, Experiment 28); round 3's worlds live through generations several times faster, so they should reach their plateau within their 3,000 iterations. Against this: their brains respond far more than B1's (How big should a brain be?), and some lines never return to behaviour they had shown, so some worlds may still climb at the end.
thesis.confirm: Both. (1) In at least 14 of the 21 worlds, the median score of the eras 500 to 3,000 against 250 (each era's score the mean of its two contests, one on each era's world) lies above the world's noise band, 0.5 plus twice the standard deviation of its twelve contests of an era against itself (250, 1,500 and 3,000, four coins each). (2) In at least 14 of the 21 worlds, the median score of the eras 1,750 to 3,000 against 1,500 lies within that band.
thesis.refute: Either: (1) in fewer than 11 of the 21 worlds do the later eras score above the band against 250, so most worlds did not get better at all; or (2) in 11 or more of the 21 the eras after 1,500 score above the band against 1,500, so most worlds were still getting better at the middle of their runs. Between the two, the thesis is undecided. A world whose contests cannot be played (its kept worlds unreadable) decides nothing, and is left out of both counts.
